newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Fincaial Times - June 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Fincaial Times - June 23.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents. For further information on these articles or details of BMC's other international press and broadcast services call Simon McMillan on +44 (0)171 256 5130 or e-mail bmc.co@ft.com -- MOBILE PHONE USERS TOLD TO CHANGE NUMBERS

A ruling by the UK telecoms watchdog, Oftel, will require the seven million British mobile phone users to change their numbers over the next four years, a declaration most operators claim is unwelcome and unnecessary. Vodafone, the largest UK mobile operator, called the announcement "unfortunate" as it would lead to confusion, while Orange Communications referred to it as "bad for customer s". Oftel are seeking all mobile numbers in the 04 range to be switched to the 07 range, and believe customers will be little effected due to constant movement between operators and the move to more efficient digital services. -- SIB AND BANK IN TALKS ON ROLES IN BANKING COLLAPSES

The Bank of England and the Securities and Investments Board (SIB) are in negotiations on how banking collapses should be dealt with once the transfer of responsibility for banking supervision is passed on to the new "super-SIB". Bank deputy governor and SIB chairman designate Howard Davies has announced the Treasury will likely publish a memorandum of understanding to resolve any misunderstanding about the organisation of banking rescues. Davies added that the new SIB would charge banks a direct fee to fund the cost of supervision and that would be balanced by reductions in the contributions made to the Bank of England. -- RETAILERS SEE LITTLE SIGN OF SPENDING SPREE

British retailers understand the need for a moderate rise in interest rates to curb consumer spending, but continue to deny that any high street boom is taking place. David Young, deputy chairman of John Lewis, and private retailer Littlewoods claim sales are "decent" and "in line with expectations" but do not agree to higher than average spending activity. Figures from the British Retail Consortium show a year-on-year slowdown in the growth in value of comsumer spending in May from 6.2 per cent in 1996 to 4.8 per cent in May 1997. -- MINISTERS TO CHALLENGE EU ON TAKEOVERS

The UK government has declared its support for London efforts to block European Union-wide legislation on the conduct of takeover bids. The issue will be debated in the European Parliament on Wednesday, where it is expected ministers from the Union will request that takeover rules be in the hands of individual member states under the principle of subsidiarity. The Takeover Panel will back government efforts, as it has lobbied for the preservation of the non-statutory system of bid regulation in the UK for some time. -- POWER GROUP TO FACE TOP-LEVEL SHAKE-UP

Anglo-French power and transport group GEC Alsthom is about to decentralise its management, in the biggest change at the organisation, run by GEC of the UK in conjunction with Alcatel Alsthom of France, since its introduction. The new business will now have a senior post of country manager in the 40 countries which are most important to its business. Among the tasks to be given to the managers will be co-ordination of group activities in national markets as well as dealings with significant customers such as government organisations. -- BSKYB TO PULL OUT OF DIGITAL TV ALLIANCE

Rupert Murdoch's British Sky Broadcasting has pulled out of the British Digital Broadcasting consortium following increased pressure by the Independent Television Commission, who were concerned BSkyB would eventually dominate both digital and satellite broadcasting in the UK. Prompting the final withdrawal by BSkyB was a compensation package of 75 million stg offered by its partners for BSkyB's 33 per cent stake if they win the three commercial licences on offer. --REUTERS CLOSES DATABASE DOORS TO MAID AND REED

London-based information company Reuters, the world's largest market data provider and news agency, has denied Maid and Reed Elsevier use of its London database as it seeks to translate its dominance in news gathering into leadership in the expanding market of online business information. In July, Reuters will launch Reuters Business Briefing, a service which will be in direct competition with Maid's profound and Reed's Lexis-Nexis, while continuing to supply Textline to groups such as Pearson of the UK. -- BG DEPUTY CHAIRMAN ON LOOKOUT FOR ANOTHER JOB

Philip Rogerson, the deputy chairman of BG Plc GAS.L, has confirmed reports that he is looking for a new job after having led BG's team in the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC) inquiry which ended next week. Saying he had no regrets about going to the MMC after rejecting Ofgas proposals, Rogerson declared he was "open to offers" about his next job, but would like an "interesting company" where he could act as chairman. -- DELTA REVIVES ZIMPLATS PLANS

Australian mining group Delta Gold has rejuvenated plans to spin off its Zimplats subsidiary and float it on the London stock exchange. Delta first considered spinning the group off in 1996, but Australian institutional shareholders objected, saying it was too soon in the development of its Hartley project in Zimbabwe to make any move. When Hartley reaches its full production capacity at the end of 1998, it will control about three per cent of the world's platinum output. -- BENETTON SET TO EXPAND IN SPORTSWEAR

Quoted Italian clothing group Benetton has announced plans to expand its sportswear and equipment business through the purchase of Benetton Sportsystem, a subsidiary of the Edizione holding company. An asset swap between the two groups would enable Edizione to pursue its diversification strategy by bidding for a five per cent stake in state-controlled motorway group Autostrade. Benetton has also announced an alliance with Deutsche Bank through which it will launch its first credit card on the Italian market.
